newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pearson in plan to buy Fairfax - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pearson in plan to buy Fairfax - paper.

text.p: British publisher Pearson Plc is part of consortium called Australian Independent Newspapers (AIN) that is considering bidding for all or part of Australian publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, The Australian newspaper said on Tuesday.

"Four representatives of AIN, plus Stephen Hill, the chief executive of the flagship Pearson title, the Financial Times, met (Australian Prime Minister John) Howard for an hour in Canberra yesterday," the newspaper said.
Howard is currently reviewing cross-media rules set up by the former Labor government which stops television station owners from controlling a major newspaper group in the same city.
Howard is widely expected to relax the rules, allowing Australian billionaire Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd to bid about A$2.5 billion for Fairfax.

The AIN consortium was based on the same group that tendered for Fairfax in 1991 and was backed by institutional shareholders Colonial Mutual, National Mutual and the Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) society, The Australian said.
"Pearson may be interested in being part of a consortium bidding for all of Fairfax or just buying the national business daily, The Australian Financial Review," the newspaper said.
"The (AIN) group is taking the view that Packer will be true to past form and bid low for Fairfax, offeirng shares in PBL, thus allowing AIN to make a better cash offer," it said.
Packer, the owner of the Nine Network via his Publishing and Broadcasting, is a 15 percent shareholder in Fairfax, the maximum currently allowed under the cross-media ownership rules now in force.
Brierley Investments Ltd is the largest shareholder in Fairfax with a 20 percent stake and is prevented under foreign investment rules from owning more than 25 percent.
